text.p: If the sight of Tiger Woods on the fairways is enough to bring his fellow professionals out in a cold sweat, then the same could be said about Britain's bookmakers who stand to lose millions if the 21-year-old lands the U.S.Open this week.

Woods, winner of the U.S. Masters in April, is favourite to complete part two of an unprecedented Grand Slam in one year which would also involve capturing the British Open and U.S. PGA championships.

One punter has staked 10,000 pounds ($16,300) at 5-1 on Woods finishing first in Bethesda, Maryland on Sunday. It is the largest ever wager on golf made in Britain. Another has bet 8,000 pounds ($13,000).
The bookmakers are predicting a 10 million pounds disaster if Woods triumphs.

Woods has also attracted a large number of bets for the Grand Slam. One man hopes for a payout of 50,000 pounds ($82,000) after staking 100 pounds ($165) at the end of last year when the odds were an incredible 5,000-1.
Other bets have been taken on Woods becoming U.S. President by the year 2020 and marrying Princess Diana -- both at 1,000-1.
